03 · Recap · Term 1 → Term 2
AY2026 · Term 2

Recap

From fine-tune first to RAG-first.

Term 1 · Sept – Dec 2025
Established the case for fine-tuning Llama-Primus-Reasoning on CCoP 2.0.
01
Foundation & setup
Local M3 evaluation infra; quantised Primus-Reasoning (8B, 4-bit) running offline.
02
CCoP 2.0 mapped
220 auditable clauses across 11 sections; IT and OT scope; ground-truth set drafted.
03
Baseline benchmarked
48.96% weighted across 17 of 21 benchmarks — reasoning 61.6%, factual grounding 31.6%.
04
Failure modes named
Hallucination of regulatory facts, scope confusion, ungrounded paraphrase.
Open question carried forward
Reasoning works; factual grounding does not. Fine-tuning encodes regulation implicitly — it cannot supply the authoritative clause text the audit requires.
PIVOT
Lead with RAG.
Quantify the lift.
Fine-tune the residual gap.
Strategic reorder · January 2026
Term 2 · Jan – Apr 2026
Reordered the program: prove RAG's contribution, then fine-tune what RAG can't fix.
01
Build RAG over CCoP 2.0
Local Qdrant hybrid search, clause-aware chunking of 8 authoritative documents, cross-encoder rerank, diagram captioning.
02
Upgrade evaluation
Dual-layer scoring — RAGAs automated quality metrics plus LLM-as-Judge for reasoning depth and hallucination.
03
Quantify native vs RAG
Same model, same ground-truth set; measure how much factual grounding retrieval recovers across 21 benchmarks.
04
Target fine-tuning to the residual
Benchmarks where RAG-augmented responses still fall short become the focused fine-tuning dataset.
Why this shape
Retrieval supplies regulatory grounding directly. Fine-tuning is reserved for what only fine-tuning can fix — making the eventual training budget defensible.

Retrieval pipeline

Seven-stage pipeline run on every query.

01

GPT-4o-mini

STAGE 02
Dual encode
BGE-large + BM25
  • ·Dense (1024-d, L2-normalised) for semantic match
  • ·Sparse for clause IDs, acronyms, exact terms

STAGE 03
Parallel prefetch
Qdrant
  • ·40 dense + 40 sparse candidates

1 / (k + rank)
  • ·Merge ranks without score normalisation
  • ·Promotes results that rank well in either list
  • ·Default k = 60

bge-reranker-large
  • ·Joint query-document attention

Parent-child merge
  • ·No threshold · no filtering before scoring

10 · RAG augmentations · Contextual RAG + HyDE
AY2026 · Term 2

Two augmentations

Augment chunks at index, queries at request.

A · INDEXING TIMEonce
Contextual RAG
Each chunk is augmented with a structural breadcrumb plus a 2–3 sentence LLM summary before embedding. Anchors the embedding in its parent context — the cross-encoder can now discriminate semantically close clauses on short queries.
Raw chunk (as parsed)5.2.2 The CIIO shall perform a periodic review of all accounts and revoke access privileges that are no longer required.
GPT-4o-mini prepends breadcrumb + context
Augmented chunk (what gets embedded)
[CCoP 2.0 → Chapter 5: Identity and
 Access Management → 5.2.2]
This clause obligates the CIIO to run
periodic account reviews and revoke
stale privileges. Search terms users
might use: "account review", "stale access", "privilege revocation".

5.2.2  The CIIO shall perform a periodic
review of all accounts and revoke
access privileges...
Effect"5.2.2" no longer ambiguous between unrelated documents · embedding sees regulatory framing
B · QUERY TIMEper request
HyDE rewrite
The user's question is rewritten as a hypothetical clause-style answer; that hypothetical is embedded for retrieval. Bridges acronym expansion and colloquial-to-formal phrasing gaps that bi-encoders cannot perform via attention.
User query (colloquial)"What are the MFA requirements?"
GPT-4o-mini rewrites in formal CCoP style
Hypothetical clause (what gets embedded)
The CIIO shall implement multi-factor authentication for all privileged
accounts accessing critical information
infrastructure systems. The Commissioner
may require additional authentication
factors where the residual risk warrants
heightened controls under Section 11(7).
Effect"MFA" → "multi-factor authentication" · embedding-space comparison is regulatory-style on both sides

Four insights
01Strong help on regulatory specifics
Four benchmarks > +0.30. B18 (governance roles +0.78), B13 (board oversight evidence +0.44), B02 (compliance classification +0.33), B21 (hallucination resistance +0.33) — all need precise CCoP text the model cannot recall from training.
02Flat where parametric memory covers it
B07, B08, B09, B10 — general risk-and-compliance reasoning the base model already handles. Retrieval neither helps nor hurts.
03Two LLM-only failures rescued by RAG
B02 and B18 score below the 15% pass threshold under Native (0.11 each). With retrieval, B02 lifts to 0.44 and B18 to 0.89.
04RAG hurts only at corpus boundaries
B23 (multi-regulator MAS/PDPA/IM8), B24 (CII Regulations 2018 forms) reference material outside the seven-document corpus; B04 is well-covered by general training. Five regressions total — all corpus-coverage, not retrieval-mechanics.

15 · Worked Example · B13-001
AY2026 · Term 2

Worked example

Sample test showing qualitative improvements using RAG.

Question · B13-001"What evidence should a Risk Manager prepare to demonstrate board cybersecurity oversight?"
Native · LLM-onlyFAILED · 0.17

Identifying Relevant Clauses. From my training knowledge, I recall that CCoP 2.0 emphasizes the importance of effective communication between management and the board regarding cybersecurity risks. Specifically, Clause 5.2.1 discusses the need for regular reporting to the board on risk management practices and their effectiveness.

Analyzing Evidence Requirements. To demonstrate board oversight, evidence should include: Risk Assessment Reports (comprehensive analyses of potential threats and vulnerabilities); Incident Response Plans (documentation showing preparedness for cyber incidents); Cybersecurity Policies (up-to-date policies that align with organizational objectives); Training Records (evidence of staff training on cybersecurity best practices).

Considering Alternative Approaches. While CCoP 2.0 focuses on the board's oversight role, it may not specify exact types of evidence. However, industry best practices suggest that regular reporting, including metrics and key performance indicators (KPIs), can effectively demonstrate oversight.

Potential Points of Failure. Without direct references to specific clauses in CCoP 2.0, there is a risk of misinterpretation. It's important to ensure the evidence aligns with both regulatory requirements and industry standards…

D1 0/3D3 0/3D6 0/3
FAILED · 0.17
RAG · HybridPASSED · 0.61

Evidence for Board Cybersecurity Oversight: To demonstrate board-level oversight of cybersecurity, a Risk Manager should prepare evidence that showcases the CIIO's compliance with regulatory requirements:

  1. Cybersecurity Risk Management Framework — outlines the organization's approach to managing cybersecurity risks, including risk assessment methodologies, roles and responsibilities, communication plans, and reporting structures.
  2. Risk Register Updates — regular updates demonstrate ongoing monitoring of identified risks and their mitigation strategies, including evidence that residual risk thresholds are not breached, as per Clause 3.2.5 of CCoP 2.0.
  3. Board Meeting Minutes — should reflect discussions on cybersecurity matters, including reviews of risk assessments, incident reports, and updates from the Cyber Incident Response Team (CIRT).
  4. Cybersecurity Reports to the Board — regular, detailed reports provided by senior management to the board, as mandated in Clause 3.2.1(d) of CCoP 2.0, should be documented.
  5. Results from Cybersecurity Exercises — documentation of scenario-based exercises (as per Clause 7.3.1), including the testing of incident response plans, business continuity plans, disaster recovery plans, and crisis communication plans.
  6. Remediation Plans and Compliance Reports — submission of remediation plans following cybersecurity exercises (Clause 7.3.5) and compliance reports to the Commissioner…

16 · Observations
AY2026 · Term 2

Observations

Where RAG helps · where it does not.

Where & why RAG helpsObs 01 · 03 · 04
01Where it helps
RAG's contribution is dimensional, not uniform
+0.086 mean lift hides a sharply non-uniform pattern. Retrieval lifts D1 verdict (+0.09), D3 grounding (+0.15), D4 scope (+0.26), D6 citation (+0.09) — the dimensions that depend on knowing the right CCoP clause and what it says. RAG is a tool for correctness against external authority, not for reasoning quality.
03Why it helps
Helps most where the topic is known but the clause is not
The four > +0.30 wins (B18, B13, B02, B21) share a property: the topic is well-represented in training, but the specific CCoP clause text is not. With retrieval, the same model with the same prompt produces the right answer — burden shifts from recall to read.
04Where it helps
Native LLM-only is structurally hazardous
Two of 18 cases (B02, B18) fell below the 15% pass threshold under Native — with confidently-asserted specifics that read as accurate citations. Confidently wrong is qualitatively worse than acknowledged uncertainty in a compliance domain. RAG removes that failure mode.
Where it fails · what's missingObs 02 · 05
02What's missing
Reasoning is solid; the gap is fact recall
D2 stability (0.593 → 0.611) is the strongest signal that the base model reasons adequately. What it lacks is reliable parametric memory of which CCoP clause says what. Future fine-tuning is best targeted at narrow factual recall, not reasoning capability.
05Where it fails
Underperforms only at corpus boundaries
Five regressions (B04, B23, B24, marginal B05 / B22) trace to corpus-coverage failures, not retrieval mechanics. B23 needs MAS / PDPA / IM8; B24 needs CII Regulations 2018 forms — material outside the seven-document corpus. The highest-leverage next step is corpus expansion.

17 · Next steps
AY2026 · Term 2

Next steps

Six work items, one sequence.

01
Ablation study using GraphRAG
Optional · exploratory
Index documents as a knowledge graph rather than flat chunks. For a regulatory corpus with cross-clause references (Cybersecurity Act §11(7); Section 7 → 8 BCP), graph-structured retrieval may surface multi-hop dependencies the flat-chunk index misses.
02
Domain-expert ground-truth confirmation
Low-risk dependency
Auditor + verifier agent pair has produced 442 verifier-approved corrections. The remaining task is human-expert sign-off across the 18 active benchmarks and the 435-case corpus — confirming, not reconstructing.
03
Re-run the full evaluation suite
After item 02
Re-execute the 18-case stratified sample plus the full 435-case corpus under both llm-only and hybrid modes once expert validation closes. Dimensional pattern and benchmark-level deltas should hold.
04
Close corpus gaps where RAG underperforms
Corpus expansion
Five RAG-negative benchmarks (B04, B23, B24, marginal B05 / B22) are corpus-coverage failures. Enumerate per benchmark — CII Regulations 2018, MAS TRM, PDPA, IM8, GovTech directives — and ingest into the retrieval index.
05
Generate fine-tuning dataset from validated GT
Term 3 prep
Use audit-corrected and expert-validated GT to derive a CCoP-aligned training set targeting the factual-recall gap. Emphasise clause-content alignment, not reasoning chains — those are already adequate.
06
Research RAFT vs vanilla QLoRA fine-tuning
Open question
RAFT (Zhang et al., 2024) trains the model on retrieved-context-plus-distractors, teaching grounding rather than memorisation. Given the production system uses retrieval at inference, is RAFT a better paradigm than vanilla QLoRA?

18 · Term 3 preview · RAFT
AY2026 · Term 2

Term 3 · A preview

Retrieval-Augmented Fine-Tuning — RAFT.

RAFT trains the model on retrieved-context-plus-distractors so it learns to ground responses in retrieved evidence and ignore noise — combining the dynamic knowledge of RAG with the domain skill that fine-tuning provides.
